import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 891

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
- [Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
- [Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture
-/

open Nat Filter Finset
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.omega

namespace Erdos891

/--
Let $2=p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes and $k\geq 2$. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large
$n$, there must exist an integer in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k)$ with $>k$ many prime factors?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_891 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + ∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime), k < ω m := by
  sorry

/--
Schinzel deduced from Pólya's theorem [Po18] (that the sequence of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded
gaps) that this is true with $p_1\cdots p_k$ replaced by $p_1\cdots p_{k-1}p_{k+1}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_891.variants.schinzel :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range (k - 1), i.nth Nat.Prime) * k.nth Nat.Prime),
      k < ω m := by
  sorry

/--
This is unknown even for $k=2$ - that is, is it true that in every interval of $6$
(sufficiently large) consecutive integers there must exist one with at least $3$ prime factors?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_891.variants.case_k_2 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ m ∈ Ico n (n + 6), 3 ≤ ω m := by
  sorry

/--
Weisenberg has observed that Dickson's conjecture implies the answer is no if we replace
$p_1\cdots p_k$ with $p_1\cdots p_k-1$. Indeed, let $L_k$ be the lowest common multiple of all
integers at most $p_1\cdots p_k$. By Dickson's conjecture [Wikipedia], there are infinitely many
$n'$ such that $\frac{L_k}{m}n'+1$ is prime for all $1\leq m < p_1\cdots p_k$. It follows that,
if $n=L_kn'+1$, then all integers in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k-1)$ have at most $k$ prime factors.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_891.variants.weisenberg (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) :
    ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∀ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime) - 1),
      ω m ≤ k := by
  sorry

end Erdos891

findings.description: The theorem at lines 73–76 has only `k` and `hk : k ≥ 2` as hypotheses, so it unconditionally asserts arbitrarily large intervals of length p₁⋯pₖ−1 whose elements all have at most k distinct prime factors. The cited result is conditional on Dickson’s conjecture. Omitting that premise changes the known conditional implication into a stronger, unconditional conjecture; the `research open` tag does not encode the missing assumption.
findings.source_evidence: The remark at https://www.erdosproblems.com/891, read in the July 9, 2026 capture https://web.archive.org/web/20260709213217id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/891, says: “Weisenberg has observed that Dickson's conjecture implies the answer is no if we replace p₁⋯pₖ with p₁⋯pₖ−1.” Its construction explicitly invokes Dickson’s conjecture to obtain infinitely many n′ for which (Lₖ/m)n′+1 is prime simultaneously. The file’s own docstring preserves this condition, but the Lean statement does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a proposition expressing Dickson’s conjecture for admissible finite families of positive-slope integer linear forms, and add it as an explicit hypothesis to this theorem. Equivalently, state `DicksonStatement → ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime) - 1), ω m ≤ k`. The existing conclusion’s quantifiers, interval endpoints, and factor-count bound can remain unchanged.

sources_consulted: T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem 891: https://www.erdosproblems.com/891. Read archived copies through https://web.archive.org/web/20260101000000id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/891 (December 21, 2025 capture) and https://web.archive.org/web/20260709213217id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/891 (July 9, 2026 capture).
Erdős Problem 891 mathematical discussion, including all three comments: https://web.archive.org/web/20260709213607id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/891.
P. Erdős and J. L. Selfridge, Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers, Illinois J. Math. 11 (1967), 428–430: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1967-21.pdf.

G. Pólya, Zur arithmetischen Untersuchung der Polynome, Math. Z. 1 (1918), 143–148. Scan: https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN266833020_0001/LOG_0020.pdf. Read the GDZ OCR for all six pages at https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/gdzocr/PPN266833020_0001/00000153.xml through 00000158.xml, especially Satz I on p. 144 and equation (14) on p. 148.

Current Erdős problem community database, entry 891: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml; database description: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md.

Bibliographic sources used to locate the primary papers: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html; https://api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=polya%201918%20arithmetischen%20polynome&rows=2; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01203608; https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/mets/PPN266833020_0001.xml.
review.notes: The other three declarations match the sources. Erdős–Selfridge p. 428 explicitly confirms the distinct-prime-factor convention. Checked prime indexing, all interval lengths, natural subtraction, boundary cases, answer scope, and filter semantics. Independent Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without warnings or errors, including the k=2 specialization and the equivalence between frequent counterexample intervals and failure of eventual success. Direct access to the Erdős site was Cloudflare-blocked; the archived page and current community database both record the problem as open. The reviewed file is unchanged.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported defect omits the Dickson-conjecture premise but leaves a substantive unconditional infinitude assertion. I have no short, independent proof or disproof of that assertion. Finite interval computations cannot establish or refute its frequently-atTop quantifier, and using the imported theorem would merely reuse its admitted proof.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created or left behind. The source-versus-statement discrepancy does not furnish a trivial mathematical proof or disproof.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported issue is a missing conjectural hypothesis, not a degeneracy making the statement trivially true or false. No short, honest demonstration of the required kind is available.

submission.summary: Added an explicit Dickson-conjecture hypothesis for admissible finite families of positive-slope integer linear forms, leaving the conclusion unchanged. Clarified the docstring and marked the known conditional implication as `research solved`. The other declarations are unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.

-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_891.variants.weisenberg
    (hdickson : ∀ (r : ℕ) (a b : Fin r → ℤ),
      (∀ i, 0 < a i) →
      (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ t : ℤ, ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a i * t + b i) →
      ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ i, (a i * (n : ℤ) + b i).natAbs.Prime)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) :
    ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∀ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime) - 1),
      ω m ≤ k := by
  sorry

end Erdos891
